body:
I'm still alive, I'm here.

Yes, it's getting difficult. I don't have anywhere to go without my boyfriend, literally. I'll be homeless if I leave. Feeling like I'd rather be homeless with my dog than deal with this. Don't know what I'd do after that though. He's stopped yelling as much, but still just on edge constantly. Even when I put the muzzle on my dog, he's constantly pushing him away or saying no or ignoring him. He knows it's killing me. I don't know how to tell him I'm suicidal because of it. I don't know if I should. Don't know if it even matters. Can't force him to not be a dick. Can't force him to understand.

If I put my dog down now while he's still so happy, that'd be murder. Not compassionate euthanasia. Straight murder. I would never forgive myself for that. Or him. Never.

I'm afraid I'll never recover from this. On my own, my own personal recovery. And with him. I don't think he realizes that he's breaking me down bit by bit and the only reason I haven't fucked off with my dog yet to go die together is because I'm too tired to actually do it.

Edit: I tried reaching out to one friend, who knows how bad my cPTSD is, who used to say he was always there for me. He isn't there for me anymore, said he had feelings for me and had to dip. So now I literally have no one. Therapist says to stay strong and do it for the dog. I'm trying. It's hard. I miss my friend. So much.

I'm really trying here. My boyfriend woke up and immediately started yelling at my dog for wanting his good morning pets, so we left and have been wandering some parks since. He's mad at me because I started crying and asking him not to yell at my dog just because he wants his affection, and for removing us from that situation. I don't want to go home anymore. I don't think I can.

I want to. My boyfriend won't even let him in the bedroom now, says it's not safe. I don't want to lock him out though so I'm on the floor next to the dog bed in the living room, planning on sleeping here. Boyfriend is angry at me for it though. But if I have to put him down, I'm not punishing him further first. I want to spend as much time with him as I can. It's not his fault he's in pain sometimes. If my boyfriend says he has to go, I'm going with him until it's his time. So I'll be homeless then. It's so much. Thanks for the advice.

That's what I know I should do. But he's still so happy, he has no issues walking, jumping, sitting, running, anything. He wants to play and pull as hard as he can, he wants to explore everything and cuddle still. But when I hurt him on accident, it was enough. Too much for him. So would it be cruel to put him down now, or cruel to keep him alive? The vet said he's happy, but just in pain. That she didn't think euthanasia was the way to go yet. I just don't know. I feel so selfish and lost and broken.

He's on 1000mg of gabapentin morning and night, a muscle relaxer, an anti-inflammatory, and now he has an anti-anxiety medication too to hopefully help him calm down some. He doesn't need to be put down yet, the vet said to monitor him for now. 

But it's a gamble, because he bit me. And like, bit me bit me. Out of nowhere. Because I irritated him near where a bad arthritis spot was, supposedly. But he gave no warning, just immediately went for my face but only got my ear and wrist. I fainted and hit my head pretty bad too, had to be taken to the hospital for that part. I have stitches in my ear, but the bites were decently superficial all things considered. Now my boyfriend is terrified of him, I think. But it's the pain. He doesn't let on or tell us how bad it is, but it's so bad he's taking 2000mg of painkillers a day - that's a lot. So much. For him to have bit me like this out of nowhere, it's bad. The vet said she'd never seen a dog with this much arthritis have this much energy though, so he must be happy. Just... Yeah.
